leading_positions.synthesis: Four of eight members (Aili, Aqvist, Chabes, Zou) put B036 first, each with the same three names (Crews, Deshaies, Handa). Shared: induced proximity to an E3 ligase as a designable chemical principle, structural confirmation of ternary complexes, and the view that approval status is not the test. Not shared: the citation wording (PROTAC concept plus cereblon glue mechanism, versus a principle-only wording), and whether Handa or Ciulli is the better third name; Zou and Aqvist name Ciulli as the main alternative, and Zou would accept Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli as second best. Aili and Chabes lean toward a single induced-proximity citation covering both PROTACs and glues. Nobody on this list has a majority of five without at least one more member. Somfai, Sparr and Linke each list B036 as an alternative (Somfai and Sparr second, Linke second), and Brzezinski lists it as an alternative.

Two members (Linke, Sparr) put B014 first with Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen. Shared: phase separation as a physical-chemical principle (multivalency, interfacial tension, demixing), a datable 2009 origin plus Rosen's quantitative phase diagrams, and 15 years of independent work. Shared reservations: the in vivo condensate debate and the exclusion of Pappu and Mittag. Sparr suggests the citation lean toward the molecular framework; Linke and Sparr both want the citation to name a principle and not claim that every condensate is a liquid. Chabes lists B014 as an alternative. Aili, Aqvist, Somfai and Zou questioned it in their responses.

One member (Somfai) puts B034 first with Buchwald and Hartwig as a two-person, mature, methods-based prize. Aqvist lists B034 as an alternative. Shared with others: clean two-person attribution and maturity. Disputed: whether the 2010 cross-coupling prize makes C-N coupling a refinement of an already honoured paradigm (Zou, Aqvist raise this) and whether Kosugi should be credited (Somfai and Zou read Kosugi's tin-amide chemistry as a precursor, Aqvist asks that it be settled from primary literature).

One member (Brzezinski) prefers a two-part prize: B067 (Gray and Winkler, electron transfer in proteins) and B066 (Shokat, covalent KRAS). This is the only two-part configuration among the eight and the only one that uses single-laureate and two-laureate parts. Others (Aili, Aqvist, Sparr, Zou) acknowledge B067's rigor and maturity but cite Marcus theory (1992) and the tunnelling-pathway theory sitting outside the credited pair. Brzezinski and Somfai list B066 as an alternative or part; B036 is Brzezinski's alternative.

areas_of_agreement: B036 is the only ballot with first-place support from more than two members, and every one of the eight members either prefers it or names it as an alternative (Aili, Aqvist, Chabes, Zou prefer it; Linke, Sparr, Somfai, Brzezinski list it as an alternative).

All members who discuss B036 accept the mechanism (E3-ligase-directed degradation, cereblon as the thalidomide target, structural ternary complexes) as scientifically established; the disagreements concern timing, attribution and citation scope.
Several members want any citation to name a principle and not a product or pipeline (Chabes, Aqvist, Linke, Sparr), and to separate original discovery from later refinement.
No member reports a conflict that would require recusal on any shortlisted candidate.

Members across different first choices agree that the three-person limit forces costly exclusions in almost every candidate: Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Kim, Ito (B036); Pappu, Mittag (B014); Dill, Bryngelson (B023); Stucky, Zhao, Inagaki (B017); Kosugi (B034).
scientific_disputes: Whether many reported in vivo condensates are equilibrium liquid-liquid phase separation or other assemblies; Linke, Sparr, Aqvist, Brzezinski, Chabes and Zou each raise this in some form, and Chabes and Zou say it keeps B014 below B036 for them. Linke and Sparr say it does not undermine the core principle.
Whether B014 is chemistry or cell biology and biophysics; Somfai asks what is new chemically, and Linke lists this as an open question.

Whether B036 should be one achievement (induced proximity to an E3 ligase) or two (PROTACs versus molecular glues, found at different times by different groups); Aili and Sparr question this, while Chabes and Aili-in-response argue that an induced-proximity citation covers both.

Whether B023 (energy landscape theory plus experiment) is treated as chemistry and whether the funnel picture is a distinct, experimentally confirmed discovery or background to the 2024 protein structure prize.
Whether B067 is a distinct achievement or an experimental extension of electron-transfer theory already honoured in 1992 (Brzezinski and others differ on this).
attribution_disputes: B036: Handa or Ciulli as third laureate beside Crews and Deshaies. Zou and Aqvist rate Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures as drug-making, Zou and Chabes view cereblon as the discovery that anchors the glue half; Sakamoto, Gray, Kim and Ito are not in any proposed trio.
B014: Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen versus a cut that includes Pappu and Mittag, with Sparr pressing for the molecular-framework contribution to be weighted more than the founding observation.
B034: whether Kosugi is a laureate-level contributor or a precursor to Buchwald and Hartwig.
B023: Wolynes, Onuchic and Fersht versus a wider group including Bryngelson and Dill, and how to divide theory and experiment.
B017: Kresge and Beck (Mobil) versus Inagaki (FSM-16), Ryoo, Stucky and Zhao; raised by Zou and Brzezinski.
B067: Gray and Winkler's share when the tunnelling-pathway theory sits partly outside the credited pair.
maturity_disputes: No PROTAC drug is approved according to several members; Aili, Aqvist, Chabes and Zou list this as a concern for B036, while Aili, Aqvist, Chabes and Zou all treat reproduced mechanism, not approval, as the relevant test. Linke and Aili ask whether B036 may be early; Chabes cannot verify current regulatory status.

Whether the 2010 cross-coupling prize (B034), the 2024 protein structure and design prize (B023), the 2025 framework materials prize (B017) and the 1992 electron-transfer prize (B067) reduce appetite for those candidates now.

Whether the in vivo condensate debate makes B014 premature or whether the principle and reconstituted systems are mature enough; B014 is more than 15 years old and B034 more than 25 by the members' own accounts.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Linke (Chair), Sparr and Somfai are Lund colleagues; all three state this is not a tie to any candidate, and Sparr says she will watch that it does not substitute for independent judgement.

Brzezinski (Secretary) works in the same field as B067 (biological electron and proton transfer) and Zou is a Stockholm University colleague of the Secretary; both state no personal or institutional connection to any credited name.
Aili notes adjacency to B058 through self-assembly and biomaterials and Sparr notes intellectual proximity to condensate and lipid-nanoparticle science; neither reports a tie to a named candidate.
Zou and Somfai note field overlap with B017 and with synthetic methodology (B034); both describe it as expertise or possible bias, not a recusal issue.
questions_for_round2: For B036, should the citation name induced proximity to an E3 ligase as one principle covering PROTACs and glues, or be limited to PROTACs; and if the former, should the third laureate beside Crews and Deshaies be Handa (cereblon) or Ciulli (VHL ligands and ternary-complex structure)?
Does the committee treat the absence of an approved PROTAC drug as a reason to defer B036, and what evidence of clinical or practical impact would the expert report need to show?

For B014, can a citation be written that rests on the physical-chemical principle and reconstituted multivalent systems without claiming that in vivo condensates are liquid phases, and does that make the case chemical enough?
For B014, should Pappu and Mittag displace Hyman or Brangwynne, or should the committee weight Rosen's molecular framework more than the 2009 observation?

Should the committee consider a two-part prize, and if so which pairings (B034 with B036, B014 with B036, or Brzezinski's B067 with B066) have a coherent joint citation and a majority of five behind both parts?
For B034, what does the primary literature say about Kosugi's work, and does the 2010 cross-coupling prize leave room for a C-N coupling prize?
Does the 2024 protein structure prize or the 2025 framework materials prize reduce the committee's appetite for B023 and B017, and what exactly separates the Mobil discovery from FSM-16 for B017?
summary.chair_observation: B036 draws first-place support from four of eight members and is named by all eight in some form, but it does not yet have the five needed for a majority and its attribution (Handa versus Ciulli, PROTAC versus glue) is not settled. B014 has two first-place supporters, including the Chair, and B034 and the B067 with B066 pair have one each. The committee agrees on the mechanism for B036 and disagrees on timing and attribution; round 2 should resolve the citation scope and third laureate for B036 and test whether any alternative can reach five on a clean citation. The Chair's own first choice, B014, is held to the same evidentiary questions as the others.
